theorems.name: func_is_wf
theorems.proof:
:= by
  rintro ⟨s, f, x, hlt, -⟩ ⟨_, _, ⟨_, _, _, _, _, _, hfs, -, -, -, -⟩, -⟩ - rfl
  exact iswf_Forall_getElem!_of_lt hfs hlt
theorems.notes: Destructures fun_func, wf_state and wf_store with rintro. Uses the first premise of fun_func_case_0 ((f.MODULE.FUNCS)[x]! < |s.FUNCS|) as the bound for the shared iswf_Forall_getElem!_of_lt. The inner bound premise is not needed.

  exact iswf_Forall_getElem!_of_lt hgs hlt
theorems.notes: Same shape as func_is_wf, using the GLOBALS Forall of wf_store and the store bound premise.

theorems.name: table_is_wf
theorems.proof:
:= by
  rintro ⟨s, f, x, hlt, -⟩ hs - rfl
  cases hs with
  | state_case_0 _ _ hst _ =>
    cases hst with
    | store_case_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ hts _ _ => exact iswf_Forall_getElem!_of_lt hts hlt
theorems.notes: Copied unchanged from SP/probes/Ex1.lean, as instructed. It compiles in Final.lean.

theorems.notes: The Forall comes from wf_frame (frame_case_). fun_local_case_0 has a single premise (x < |f.LOCALS|), which is used as the bound.

theorems.name: with_global_is_wf
theorems.proof:
:= by
  rintro ⟨s, f, x, v, -⟩ hs - hv rfl
  cases hs with
  | state_case_0 _ _ hst hf =>
    cases hst with
    | store_case_ fs gs ts ms es ds hfs hgs hts hms hds =>
      refine wf_state.state_case_0 _ _ (wf_store.store_case_ _ _ _ _ _ _ hfs ?_ hts hms hds) hf
      exact iswf_Forall_modify _ (fun g hg => by
        cases hg with | globalinst_case_ gt0 _ _ => exact wf_globalinst.globalinst_case_ gt0 _ hv) gs _ hgs
theorems.notes: Copied unchanged from SP/probes/Ex1.lean, as instructed. It compiles in Final.lean.

theorems.name: with_table_is_wf
theorems.proof:
:= by
  rintro ⟨s, f, x, i, r, -⟩ ⟨_, _, ⟨_, _, _, _, _, _, hfs, hgs, hts, hms, hds⟩, hf⟩ - rfl
  refine wf_state.state_case_0 _ _ (wf_store.store_case_ _ _ _ _ _ _ hfs hgs ?_ hms hds) hf
  exact iswf_Forall_modify _ (fun _ ⟨tt, _, htt⟩ => wf_tableinst.tableinst_case_ tt _ htt) _ _ hts
theorems.notes: The theorem has no wf premise on v_ref. It is still provable because wf_tableinst constrains only TYPE, not REFS. iswf_Forall_modify works for any index, so the getElem! store index needs no bound and the relation's bound premise is cleared.

theorems.name: with_tableinst_is_wf
theorems.proof:
:= by
  rintro ⟨s, f, x, ti, -⟩ ⟨_, _, ⟨_, _, _, _, _, _, hfs, hgs, hts, hms, hds⟩, hf⟩ - hti rfl
  exact wf_state.state_case_0 _ _
    (wf_store.store_case_ _ _ _ _ _ _ hfs hgs (iswf_Forall_modify _ (fun _ _ => hti) _ _ hts) hms hds) hf
theorems.notes: The update function is constant (fun _ => ti), so wf_tableinst ti closes each element. The proof does not depend on the index.

theorems.name: with_mem_is_wf
theorems.proof:
:= by
  rintro ⟨s, f, x, i, j, bs, -⟩ ⟨_, _, ⟨_, _, _, _, _, _, hfs, hgs, hts, hms, hds⟩, hf⟩ - hb rfl
  refine wf_state.state_case_0 _ _ (wf_store.store_case_ _ _ _ _ _ _ hfs hgs hts ?_ hds) hf
  exact iswf_Forall_modify _
    (fun _ ⟨mt, _, hmt, hbs⟩ => wf_meminst.meminst_case_ mt _ hmt (iswf_Forall_splice _ _ _ hbs hb)) _ _ hms
theorems.notes: Uses the ported helper iswf_Forall_splice, which is not in the probe module. The second Nat argument (j / nat_0) is unused by fun_with_mem.

theorems.name: with_data_is_wf
theorems.proof:

theorems.notes: datainst has the single field BYTES, so {elem with BYTES := bs} is just {BYTES := bs}, and wf_datainst.datainst_case_ applied to the byte premise closes it.

theorems.name: instexport_is_wf
theorems.proof:
:= by
  rintro h ⟨nm, xi, hn, -⟩ rfl
  cases h <;> exact wf_exportinst.exportinst_case_ _ _ hn
theorems.notes: All four fun_instexport cases are closed by the wf_name premise from wf_export. wf_exportinst does not constrain ADDR, so the bound premise and the getElem! address are irrelevant. Axioms: [propext] only.

helpers.name: iswf_Forall_splice
helpers.text:
theorem iswf_Forall_splice {α : Type} {P : α → Prop} (l u : List α) (i : Nat) :
    Forall P l → Forall P u → Forall P (splice l u i) := by
  intro hl hu
  unfold splice
  refine iswf_Forall_append (iswf_Forall_append ?_ ?_) ?_
  · exact fun x hx => hl x (List.mem_of_mem_take hx)
  · exact fun x hx => hu x (List.mem_of_mem_take hx)
  · exact fun x hx => hl x (List.mem_of_mem_drop hx)
helpers.notes: Ported unchanged (same name and statement) from the old helper in OLD_wasm2.0.lean, so it stays compatible if another agent ports it too. The name occurs nowhere in SP/work/probe_module_wasm2.0.lean. It depends only on splice (line 12 of the model) and the existing helper iswf_Forall_append. Its only user here is with_mem_is_wf, so place it directly above that theorem. It is independent of any Inhabited default.

issues: No false or unprovable statements, and no theorem needs an Inhabited default value. The accessor proofs use only the store-bound premise through iswf_Forall_getElem!_of_lt. The with_* proofs use iswf_Forall_modify, which holds for every index, so the getElem! store index (f.MODULE.X)[x]! never has to be evaluated or bounded.

Model behaviour (not a blocker): with_table_is_wf has no wf_ref premise, and with_elem_is_wf has no premise on the new ref list. Both are provable only because wf_tableinst constrains TYPE alone (not REFS) and wf_store puts no condition on ELEMS. The model has no wf_eleminst predicate at all.

Model behaviour: each fun_with_* relation bounds only proj_uN_0 x < |f.MODULE.X|, not the store address (f.MODULE.X)[x]! < |s.X|. An out-of-range address therefore makes List.modify a no-op instead of being rejected. Well-formedness is preserved either way, and the proofs clear the bound premise.

Model behaviour: fun_with_mem takes two Nat arguments (i, j) but only uses i (splice elem.BYTES b_lst i). The slice end j from the spec's BYTES[i : j] is dropped by the translation, because splice caps by payload length instead. This does not affect wf.

Helper bookkeeping: iswf_Forall_splice is ported from OLD_wasm2.0.lean with the same name and statement; it is the only new helper. The proofs also use the existing helpers iswf_Forall_modify (already above with_local_is_wf in the probe module, hence above every with_* theorem), iswf_Forall_append, and the shared iswf_Forall_getElem!_of_lt.
